raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`graph_capture()` creates a new `torch.cuda.Stream` on every call. As a result, each capture pass (CUDA-graph memory profiling, model capture, speculator capture, encoder capture) runs on its own stream. PyTorch allocates a 32 MiB cuBLAS workspace for each stream at its first GEMM and keeps it until the process exits. Each extra capture stream therefore holds another 32 MiB, plus any other per-stream kernel state (for example DeepGEMM mHC barriers on DeepSeek-V4.1). This memory stays allocated while awake and is one of the untagged leftovers that survive `sleep()` (#59055).

This PR caches one capture stream per device. Every `graph_capture()` caller (`cudagraph_utils.py`, `encoder_runner.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`) runs one after another on the worker thread, and the calls are never nested, so one stream per device is enough.

One thing for reviewers: PyTorch's `CUDAGraph::reset()` calls `clearCublasWorkspacesForStream()` on the graph's capture stream. With one shared stream, destroying any graph frees the workspace that every graph on that stream uses. Every current destruction path destroys all graphs together and does so before any recapture: profiling teardown happens before the real capture (and `freeze_gc_for_cudagraph_capture` runs `gc.collect()` first), elastic EP's `release_graphs()` clears the model and speculator graphs together, and shutdown destroys everything. On GB300 I checked after serving that the capture stream still held the same workspace (touching the handle allocated 0 bytes).

Why this is not a duplicate: no open PR changes the stream used by `graph_capture()`. #52553 deals with FlashInfer's GEMM workspace, not the per-stream cuBLAS workspace.

## Test Plan

- New CPU unit test `tests/distributed/test_utils.py::test_graph_capture_reuses_stream`.
- On 4x H200 in the CI image, with this branch's Python code on top: `tests/v1/cudagraph`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`, `tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py`, `tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`, `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`, `tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py`.
- On 4x GB300: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + MTP with `--enable-sleep-mode`, on the nightly image with the sleep-mode stack (#59156, #59158, #59160, #59228) applied, with and without this change.
  - A 553-request round before sleep, compared token by token with the same round after wake.
  - 22 sleep/wake cycles, alternating full and selective wake. Each cycle runs a 64-request subset; every 10th cycle runs the full round.
  - Live 33,554,432-byte blocks outside any cuMem pool, counted from `torch.cuda.memory_snapshot()`.

## Test Result

- New unit test: 1 passed.
- `test_custom_all_reduce.py`: 50 passed, 1 skipped. `test_pynccl.py`: 15 passed. `test_pp_cudagraph.py`: 1 passed. `test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`: 13 passed. `test_cumem.py`: 12 passed.
- `tests/v1/cudagraph`: 108 passed, 14 failed. All 14 failures are in `test_cudagraph_mode.py` and happen at model load, because the offline HF cache on the test machine has no weights for `Qwen/Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct`. I have not rerun these tests with the weights available.
- `test_sleep_mode.py`: 8 passed, 1 failed. The failing test is `test_deep_sleep_compressed_tensors_kv_scales`, whose model is not in the offline cache. Unmodified main fails it the same way.
- GB300, V4-Flash TP4 + MTP:
  - Before sleep vs. after wake: 553/553 identical, and memory changed by 0 MiB on all 4 GPUs.
  - 22/22 cycles bit-identical, with asleep and awake memory flat across cycles.
  - Untagged 32 MiB blocks per GPU: 5. An earlier snapshot of the same stack without this change had 6.
  - Asleep: 6249/6377/6377/6249 MiB per GPU, compared with 6313/6439 MiB for the stack without this change, a saving of 64 MiB per GPU. The run without the change is from an earlier launch on another node of the same type.

AI assistance was used for this PR (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests.

### Re-check on current main (`bdd31c31d`), GB300 (supersedes the earlier GB300 figure)

Re-checked on main bdd31c31d (applies cleanly), 4x GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + MTP,
--enable-sleep-mode, default V2 model runner, two launches each with and without this PR:
- Unit test: 1 passed, 3 runs (fails on main).
- CUDA graph capture memory: 5.56 GiB -> 4.94 GiB per GPU in every launch, so the KV
  cache grows from 201.51 to 202.13 GiB.
- Asleep: 10525 MiB/GPU in both launches with this PR vs 10869-11321 MiB/GPU on main
  (main's launches differ by a constant 452 MiB step unrelated to this PR), i.e. at
  least 344 MiB/GPU less.
- 3 sleep/wake cycles: 28/28 greedy and 28/28 seeded top-k/top-p outputs identical to
  the awake reference after every wake; wake 1.08-1.26 s (main 1.06-1.31 s).
